title: CRLR/969/2023 of X Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.969 of 2023
X ...Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Pooran Singh Rawat, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Akshay Latwal, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
followings:-
(i) The order dated 31.10.2020, passed by the
Juvenile Justice Board, Champawat ("JJB")
in Bail Application No. 05 of 2023, X Vs.
State, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC and
Section 5j(ii)/6 of the Protection of Children
from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ("the Act"),
Police Station Lohaghat, District
Champawat of the revisionist has been
rejected and;
(ii) The judgment and order dated 16.11.2023,
passed in Criminal Appeal No.40 of 2023, by
the Child Court/Special Session Judge,
Champawat ("the Appeal"). By it, the appeal

2
of the revisionist has been rejected and the
order passed by the JJB has been upheld.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the file.
3. The revisionist is a child in conflict with law
(CIL).
4. According to the FIR, the CIL established physical
relations with victim, a young girl of 16 years, due to which,
she got pregnant. Her foetus was aborted.
5. Learned counsel for the CIL would submit that
the CIL is in jail for more than six months. The prosecution
story is not believable.
6. Learned State counsel would submit that the
victim has supported the prosecution case in her statement
under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
("the Code").
7. The revisionist is a CIL. The bail for a CIL, all the
offences are bailable irrespective of its being classified
bailable or non bailable in the Code. A CIL is entitled to bail
subject to riders as given under Section 12 of the Juvenile
Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 ("the
Act"). Bail to the CIL may be denied if there appear
reasonable grounds for believing that it is likely to bring the

3
association to any known criminal or expose him to moral,
physical or psychological danger or his release would defeat
the ends of justice. The principles that govern the Act are
given under Section 3 of the Act. The principle of best
interest, the principle of family responsibility and the
principle of innocence are some of them. According to the
one of the principles, the primary responsibility of care,
nurture and protection of the child shall be that of the
biological family or adoptive or foster parents, as the case
may be.
8. The victim in the instant case has been examined
under Section 164 of the Code. She and the applicant, both
were in the relationship. The victim got pregnant. The social
investigation report is on record. It does not reveal anything
adverse against the CIL. It is satisfactory. It also records
that the CIL and the victim both were in the relationship.
9. Having considered, the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that in this case, there is no impediment
in grant of bail to the CIL. Accordingly, the revision deserves
to be allowed.
10. The revision is allowed. The judgment and orders
are set aside.
11. The CIL be given into the custody of his father
subject to production of two reliable sureties. The father of

4
the CIL shall also give an undertaking that he shall take
care of the CIL and shall not allow him to contact any of the
witnesses or their family members. The father of the CIL
shall also undertake that he shall also not contact either the
witnesses or any of their family members.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 18.04.2024
Ravi
